messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the 6.2 kernel roll in eu-west, ~12 GPU hosts started showing NVLINK flaps and sporadic OOMs during batch inference. Rolling back one host now to confirm.
jason: ugh. Which driver/CUDA combo are those nodes on? did we change any driver modules in the image? :grimacing:
ekaterina: They were on nvidia-driver 525 + CUDA 11.8 image (the standard stable image). Kernel was moved from 5.15.0-102 to 6.2.8-rc1 for security backport.
maya: exact dmesg on one host — `dmesg | tail` showed:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568001] nvidia: timeout waiting for memory ops
[ 1234.568102] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 8421 (python) total-vm:2563456k
```
sam: NVLINK flapping + OOM + GPU fall-off usually points to driver <-> kernel ABI mismatch. Did we rebuild the nvidia module for the 6.2 kernel? infra-bot: scheduled kernel-upgrade job #382 completed on 12 hosts, module rebuild attempted via dkms on 0 hosts.
jason: dkms failing would do it. Can you paste `modinfo nvidia` and `uname -r` from a broken host? may help confirm taint/abi mismatch.
maya: from broken host:
```
uname -r: 6.2.8-rc1
modinfo nvidia
filename: /lib/modules/5.15.0-102/updates/dkms/nvidia.ko
version: 525.105.17
license: NVIDIA
```
maya: so the nvidia module still points at the old kernel's path.
ekaterina: Looks like the kernel upgrade path didn't trigger our post-install dkms rebuild hook — probably because we used a custom kernel packaging flow for the region and missed a symlink. On the surface that's a packaging bug, but we also need to confirm the 525 driver actually supports 6.2.
sam: quick check on support matrix: 525 series has some 6.x patches but not fully validated. 530+ is recommended for 6.2 in vendor notes.
ops-oncall: rolling back the eu-west batch to 5.15 now. Moving traffic off those hosts. ETA 8m.
maya: thanks — I put a temporary capacity cap and marked the nodes draining.
jason: long-term fixes:
- verify kernel packaging triggers dkms/module rebuild
- test driver 525 vs 6.2 in staging (preferably on same NV hw)
- consider pinning kernel for dedicated GPU fleet until driver is validated
- update runbook for `NVRM: Xid 79` to include modinfo/uname checks

ekaterina: also noticed increased NCCL timeouts on multi-GPU jobs before the OOMs. Possibly NVLINK connectivity flapping caused worker retries and memory accumulation.
sam: can someone capture `nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS,PEER_TO_PEER` and `dmesg -T` from a problematic host before we reboot it? we need to send a bundle to vendor if it persists.
maya: grabbing logs now and uploading to /mnt/shared/incident/1769876543. I'll include kernel packages and apt history.
infra-bot: incident ticket INF-2026-309 created, priority P1. Assigned: eng-infra.
ops-oncall: after rollback, two hosts still showing intermittent GPU disconnects — isolating to one rack (rack-12). Might be cabling/IOH at the rack level. Scheduling hardware triage for rack-12 at 1500 UTC.
jason: good catch. If it's only rack-12, we should pause further kernel rollouts to hosts mapped to that rack until triage completes.
ekaterina: agree. Also notify platform teams to avoid concurrent CUDA/driver upgrades while kernel is in flight.
maya: notes for follow-up: run staged test matrix in staging cluster covering kernel 5.15/6.0/6.2 x driver 515/525/530 x CUDA 11.8/12.1, run small NCCL collective stress for 30m. Will draft a PR for gating rollouts.
sam: FYI — cost impact: draining + draining fallback to other regions will increase burst GPU spend by ~18% for next 24h. Finance pinged.
ops-oncall: I'll coordinate with oncall-hw for physical checks. tagging @oncall for hardware window.
maya: I'll keep thread updated as we get logs and results from triage. Thanks team :thumbsup:
